submission.justification:
Crystal-K3 at 5.5 cm thickness is recommended as the optimal scintillator configuration for the gamma spectrometer. This configuration achieves the best energy resolution (4.377%) at 662 keV among all viable candidates while meeting all low-background requirements.

Key findings from the analysis:
1. Background screening eliminated Crystal-K1 (2 counts/kg/day exceeds the 0.5 counts/kg/day budget by 4x), leaving K2 and K3 as viable low-background candidates.
2. Crystal-K2, despite having the lowest background (0.1 counts/kg/day), exhibits significantly inferior energy resolution (8.811% at best) due to its lower light yield ranking (#1).
3. Crystal-K3 combines excellent low-background performance (0.3 counts/kg/day, 40% margin below budget) with superior energy resolution, making it the clear choice.
4. Thickness optimization through systematic simulation showed that 5.5 cm delivers the best resolution (4.377%) for K3, compared to 4.488% at 5 cm and degraded performance at other thicknesses.

This configuration achieves 2.0x better energy resolution than the only alternative low-background option (K2), which is critical for the facility's assay programme requiring precise gamma spectroscopy of construction materials for dark-matter experiment screening.
